subject.title: Gateway restart failure should keep previous instance running to avoid total disconnect

question: Should OpenClaw support old-listener-preserving gateway restarts across managed and unmanaged supervisors, and what scope should be guaranteed first?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix changes gateway lifecycle semantics across service managers, locks, ports, channel connections, rollback, and notification behavior.

options.title: Design atomic restart continuity
options.body: Specify the minimal supported supervisor and port/lock handoff contract, then implement replacement health verification before making the current gateway unreachable.

options.title: Limit to recovery and diagnostics
options.body: Keep current restart ordering but improve doctor/status/channel notifications so failed restarts are visible and recoverable without promising atomic availability.

options.title: Defer as unsupported
options.body: Document that restarts can temporarily disconnect the gateway and require operator access for recovery after failed startup.

recommendation.title: Design atomic restart continuity
recommendation.body: Specify the minimal supported supervisor and port/lock handoff contract, then implement replacement health verification before making the current gateway unreachable.

likelyOwner.reason: Current restart lifecycle blame and daemon lifecycle history make this the strongest routing candidate for the product/architecture decision.
